content.user_title: Generate SQL Queries for DBX Studio
content.value_statement: Database users need reliable SQL that matches their connection type and schema. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to inspect schemas, write read-only queries, and explain results clearly.
actual_capabilities: Writes SQL for PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, MySQL, and SQLite.
Encourages schema inspection before writing queries.
Adds result limits unless the user asks for all rows.
Uses SELECT and WITH query patterns for read-only analysis.
Formats identifiers and query examples for DBX Studio workflows.
Supports aggregations, CTEs, window functions, and chart generation guidance.
limitations: Does not define or install the DBX Studio tools it references.
Cannot verify live schemas without access to the user database connection.
Does not support INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, or DDL query workflows.
May need user confirmation for dialect-specific functions or permissions.

use_cases.title: Explore a New Database
use_cases.description: Inspect tables, preview rows, and create safe starter queries before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Build Reporting Queries
use_cases.description: Create CTEs, aggregations, and window functions for dashboards or recurring reports.

use_cases.title: Debug SQL Results
use_cases.description: Review schema assumptions, quote identifiers, and adjust SQL for the selected database dialect.

prompt_templates.title: List Available Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DBX Studio schema tools to show the tables available in my current connection. Summarize the main tables and likely join keys.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Safe Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a read-only query that shows recent orders by month. Check the schema first, use the correct dialect, and add a sensible limit.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Report Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this reporting question and build an efficient SQL query with CTEs if needed. Explain any assumptions about columns or filters.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Complex Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use schema inspection and read-only SQL to calculate retention by cohort. Include the query logic, key assumptions, and chart recommendations.

output_examples.input: Show monthly revenue for completed orders.
output_examples.output: The assistant inspects the schema, identifies the orders table, and returns a limited monthly revenue summary with clear totals.
The assistant suggests a CTE with a row number window function and explains how it selects the latest transaction per user.

output_examples.input: Why does my query fail in BigQuery?
output_examples.output: The assistant checks identifier quoting and date functions, then explains dialect changes needed for BigQuery.

best_practices: Inspect schema and column names before writing SQL.
Keep queries read-only and include limits for exploratory work.
State dialect assumptions and explain important filters or joins.
anti_patterns: Running broad queries before checking schema and row volume.
Using write operations or DDL through an exploratory assistant.
Copying SQL between dialects without checking function differences.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, MySQL, and SQLite.

faq.question: Can it change database records?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the assistant to use SELECT and WITH queries only.

faq.question: Does it need access to my database?
faq.answer: It needs DBX Studio connection tools to inspect schemas or run read-only queries.

faq.question: Can it show the SQL it used?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill says to show SQL when the user asks how the result was produced.

faq.question: Does it add limits automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the assistant to add limits unless the user explicitly asks for all rows.

faq.question: Is it useful for query optimization?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide CTEs, aggregations, window functions, and dialect-specific adjustments.
